finalists.label: Pilonidal sinus
finalists.why: The presence of a small superior sinus tract without obvious pits and mild serous discharge strongly supports this diagnosis.

finalists.label: Psoriasis
finalists.why: The patient's history of inverse psoriasis affecting the natal cleft is a specific finding that supports this diagnosis.

finalists.label: Chronic Wound
finalists.why: The chronic superficial sacral wound present for approximately 2 years and the broad area of excoriated skin with plaques and focal ulceration in the upper natal cleft support this diagnosis.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a small superior sinus tract without obvious pits and mild serous discharge, along with the chronic superficial sacral wound, decided the final comparison in favor of Pilonidal sinus.
